item.title: Why is OnInitializedAsync() Called Twice .NET 8 Blazor?
item.description:
Why is OnInitializedAsync() Called Twice on Page Reload in .NET 8 Blazor?

Top 5 Methods to Handle OnInitializedAsync() Being Called Twice in .NET 8 Blazor

- Solve-Multiple-OnInitializedAsync-Calls

In Blazor applications, particularly with .NET 8, it’s common to experience OnInitializedAsync() being called twice. This happens when using the RenderMode.InteractiveServer, which triggers the method once during prerendering and again after the server establishes a connection. This double execution can impact performance and lead to repeated database queries or unnecessary operations.

item.title: Top 5 Steps to Fix JavaScript Interop Errors in Blazor
item.description:
JavaScript interop issues in Blazor often arise when attempting to access local storage during the wrong lifecycle phase. This commonly occurs in Blazor Server-side projects where prerendering is enabled. In this guide, we’ll explore the top 5 steps to resolve these errors effectively.

Step 1: Identify the Problem Area in the Lifecycle

The most common issue stems from making JavaScript interop calls outside the OnAfterRenderAsync method, which is where interop is safely performed during prerendering. The error JavaScript interop calls cannot be issued at this time indicates an improper lifecycle phase for executing JavaScript interop calls.

item.title: Top 5 Steps to Add Authentication in a Blazor Web App (.NET 8 SSR)
item.description:
Top 5 Steps to Add Authentication in a Blazor Web App (.NET 8 SSR)

Blazor has become a go-to framework for building interactive web UIs using C#. With the advent of .NET 8, there are new templates and features, including Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for Blazor. In this guide, we’ll walk you through the process of adding authentication to a Blazor Web App (SSR) using the command-line interface (CLI). This is especially useful for developers looking to secure their applications with individual accounts.

item.title: How to Resolve MissingMethodException in Blazor Server-Side Projects
item.description:
4 Steps to Resolve MissingMethodException in Blazor Server-Side Projects

When working with Blazor Server applications, particularly when implementing dependency injection, you might encounter the frustrating MissingMethodException. This issue typically arises when Blazor cannot instantiate a component because it lacks a parameterless constructor. In this guide, we will explore how to resolve this issue effectively.

Blazor components are initialized by the framework, which requires a parameterless constructor for dynamic instantiation. If your component has a constructor with parameters (e.g., for dependency injection), Blazor won’t know how to create an instance, leading to the MissingMethodException. Here’s how you can address this issue step-by-step.
